title: Developer onramp mini-projects: opinionated starter templates for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, and CLI with retry & streaming patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: provide a set of tiny, production-adjacent mini-projects (Next.js frontend, FastAPI backend, Go HTTP server, and a small CLI) that demonstrate: 1) idiomatic usage of Redwood SDKs across Python/TS/Go, 2) robust retry policies and idempotency patterns, 3) streaming ergonomics (client & server), 4) local dev workflow and CI-friendly smoke tests, and 5) cost-conscious defaults (batching, short sequence heuristics). These should be opinionated: small repo per example, clear README, one canonical prompt set, e2e test that asserts basic correctness and latency under a simulated stubbed runtime.

Why: teams repeatedly ask for runnable end-to-end examples that they can fork and modify. Existing cookbook snippets are fragments; this ticket creates cohesive mini-projects that show end-to-end concerns (network timeouts, backpressure, graceful cancellation, metrics hooks) and reduce onboarding time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Four repos in the examples folder (nextjs, fastapi, go-http, cli) with minimal Dockerfile + dev server instructions.
- Each repo includes:
  - README with quickstart (local dev using a lightweight local mock or Redwood dev token), feature list, and configuration notes for Dedicated/Private.
  - One example showing streaming responses with client-side consumption and cancellation (Next.js streaming SSR/edge example using fetch+readableStream; FastAPI using async generators; Go showing net/http flusher-based streaming). TS/Python/Go client snippets use the official SDKs.
  - Retry wrapper pattern (exponential backoff, jitter, idempotency key example for non-idempotent endpoints, and detection of retriable error classes). Include server-side idempotency echo for CLI/Go example.
  - A small test harness that verifies retry behavior by simulating transient 502/504 responses and ensuring client eventually succeeds according to policy.
  - A brief section on cost & performance guidance: batch size defaults, recommended sequence length caps, and when to enable prefix/KV caching.
- One consolidated top-level README explaining when to pick each mini-project and links to SDK reference, console rollout docs, and the runtime perf checklist.
- CI job that runs the smoke e2e for each mini-project (can use the mock emitter) and fails on regressions.

Technical approach and notes:
- Streaming ergonomics: prefer ReadableStream (browser) and async iterator (Python) and channel-based streaming (Go). Provide thin helpers in each example to convert SDK streaming responses into native primitives (ReadableStream -> JSX streaming page; async iterator -> FastAPI server-sent-events; Go -> http.Flusher push). Emphasize backpressure handling (buffering small chunks, avoid unlimited accumulation). Show a resumable consumer pattern for the CLI that can restart from last token using a persisted conversation cursor.
- Retries: implement an SDK-agnostic retry wrapper in each language that accepts policy (max_retries, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter_pct). Demonstrate a safe default policy (3 retries, capped at 2s) and an aggressive low-latency policy for interactive flows (1 retry, low delay). For non-idempotent operations show generating idempotency-key header and server-side simple dedupe table (in-memory for example). Document trade-offs: more aggressive retries increase perceived reliability but can double-cost and duplicate side effects if idempotency is not used.
- Local dev: include a lightweight mock server (node/python binary) that can be toggled to return streaming responses, transient errors, or inject latency. Provide a script to run all examples against the mock without requiring Redwood credentials.
- Security: do not embed real API tokens. Use .env.example with instructions for Redwood dev token and env var names. Note: security review not required for examples but follow safe patterns in READMEs.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Monorepo vs multiple tiny repos: prefer multiple tiny folders under examples/ (keeps CI focused) but share a common scripts/ for test harness to avoid duplication.
- How deep to integrate with Console telemetry: include guidance and example env var to enable telemetry (REDWOOD_TRACE_ENDPOINT) but do not send real telemetry from CI by default.
- Streaming format: use newline-delimited JSON chunking for cross-language simplicity in addition to native SDK streaming for best-practice example.

Tasks (implementation checklist):
- Create examples/next-mini (Next.js app) + README + streaming page + client helper (Diego)
- Create examples/fastapi-mini (FastAPI server + async client example) (Ava)
- Create examples/go-mini (Go HTTP server + simple client + idempotency example) (Jordan)
- Create examples/cli-mini (minimal CLI showing resumable streaming and idempotency) (Nina)
- Create examples/mock-server (configurable behavior) and shared test harness (Sahil)
- Write consolidated README, CI matrix, and cost guidance doc (Diego)
- Add PR template and checklist for examples (include testing on Dedicated/private notes) (Ava)

Delivery plan:
- Week 1: skeletons + mock server + one green example (Next.js streaming page) for early review.
- Week 2: remaining examples, test harness, and consolidated docs.
- Week 3: polish, performance notes, and user testing with two internal teams.
